1  MFA No. 8380 of 2022  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the order dated 16.04.2022 in M.V.C.No.40/2019 passed by Court of Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Kollegala, petitioner therein has preferred the present appeal.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24.09.2018 at about 5.15 a.m. the petitioner was traveling as a passenger from Kollegala to Malavalli in a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-10-F-0446.

When the bus reached near Siddharthanagara, 5th Cross of Malavalli town, the driver of the bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against one Mahadeva and then hit an electric pole, because of which, the petitioner sustained the fracture of L1 vertebra and lateral end of clavicle bone.

4. The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.2,86,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till realization under the following heads:
Towards pain and sufferings Rs.15,000/-
Towards medical expenses Rs. Nil

Towards diet, food, nourishment,
 attendant, conveyance charges and Rs.5,000/-
 other expenses

Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of permanent physical Rs.2,45,700/- disability Loss of amenities of life and discomfort Rs.10,000/- Loss of income during laid up period Rs.10,500/-
 Future medical expenses Rs. Nil
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident happened in the year 2018.
The petitioner has not proved his income before the Tribunal.

Hence, as per Lok Adalat chart, the same is considered at Rs.12,500/- per K Rajashankaramurthy @ vs The Divisional Controller on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68850463/
2 month.

sentences.text: The petitioner was aged 46 years at the time of the accident and has suffered a total body disability of 15%.

Given his age, a multiplier of 13 is adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text:
Thus, towards 'loss of future income due to permanent disability', the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.2,92,500/- (Rs.12,500/- x 12 x 13 x 15%).
6.

Given the nature of injuries, three months has to be considered as laid up period and the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.37,500/- (Rs.12,500/- x 3) towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
7.
Towards pain and suffering, Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I am of the opinion that the same requires to be enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Towards 'medical expenses', it is submitted that the petitioner took free treatment in government hospital and hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'diet, food, nourishment, attendant, conveyance charges and other expenses' a sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded.
Taking into consideration the nature of injuries and the time spent in the hospital, the same is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life and discomfort', a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.30,000/-.

Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads are modified as hereunder:-
Towards pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/-

Towards diet, food, nourishment,
 attendant, conveyance charges and Rs.10,000/-
 other expenses
Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of permanent physical Rs.2,92,500/- disability Loss of amenities of life and discomfort Rs.30,000/-

Loss of income during laid up period Rs.37,500/-
 TOTAL Rs.4,20,000/-
 Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.4,20,000/- as against Rs.2,86,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Further, given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,33,800/- (Rs.4,20,000/-
minus Rs.2,86,200/-) from the date of petition before the Tribunal till realization.

Hence, the following:
ORDER K Rajashankaramurthy @ vs The Divisional Controller on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68850463/
3 i) The appeal is allowed in part.
